title: Memory coagulation: runtime allocator + KV reclamation fix and customer escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported recurring GPU OOMs during sustained chat/streaming workloads. Investigation shows a KV cache handle reclamation race combined with allocator slab fragmentation leads to long-lived unreachable allocations (we call this 'memory coagulation') that steadily grow until OOM. Symptoms: slow memory growth over hours, degraded tail latency, then sudden OOMs under burst. Customers observed this on both Ampere and Hopper fleets; Dedicated pools saw faster degradation due to larger session counts.
reproduction_steps: 1) Run sustained multitenant chat workload with 1000 concurrent short sessions (seq_len skewed to 1-64)
2) Enable prefix KV caching and use model variants with low quantization (int8) on GPU nodes
3) Observe memory growth over 4-8 hours then OOM tracer shows stale KV handles and non-reclaimed arena slabs
root_cause_summary: Race in KV handle reclamation: eviction path marks entries but deferred free path can miss references when compaction runs concurrently
Allocator fragmentation: small allocations from session metadata and per-token scratch are not coalesced leading to many tiny free chunks that the GPU allocator cannot reuse efficiently
Workload interaction: continuous streaming + small seq length increases frequency of KV churn exposing the races
short_term_mitigations: 1) Force periodic KV drain in affected clusters (cron job) to accelerate reclamation
2) Apply temporary conservative autoscaling guard: reduce max_concurrent_sessions_per_gpu by 30% for Dedicated customers showing growth
3) Patch hosted routing to prefer model variant with lower memory footprint until runtime rollout completes
4) Add emergency pod eviction schedule to reclaim whole process on detection of >85% GPU memory sustained for 15m
long_term_fix_summary: A) Introduce epoch-based KV handle lifecycle: on eviction mark epoch and defer reclamation until safe sync point
B) Implement allocator coalescing pass during low-load windows to merge adjacent free regions on GPU arena
C) Strengthen compaction handshake between KV index and allocator to avoid stale pointer windows
D) Add pruning heuristics for tiny session allocations and move them to slab pools sized for short-lived objects
implementation_notes: - New epoch counter stored in runtime header; reclamation only proceeds when node advances epoch consensus
- Coalescer implemented as background worker that yields to serving threads and bounded to N MB/s of maintenance work
- Add unit + stress tests that simulate interleaved eviction+compaction with randomized timing
- Telemetry: expose kv_epoch_lag, coalescer_throughput, reclaimed_slabs_count to console
acceptance_criteria: - Reproduction workload no longer leads to OOM after 24h in CI stress harness
- Memory growth rate reduced to <5% over 8h under production-like load
- No regression in median latency (+/-5%) on canary pool
- New metrics reported in Console and alerted in SRE runbooks
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime patch behind feature flag and ship to internal canary Dedicated pool (low impact customers)
2) Monitor kv_epoch_lag and reclaimed_slabs_count for 48h, rollback if kv_epoch_lag increases >20% or tail latency regresses >10%
3) Expand to hosted pool canary across two regions after 72h of clean signals
4) Offer opt-in to Private customers for patch build; plan air-gap packaging and compatibility notes
5) Full fleet rollout after 7 days of stable canaries with staged ramp-up (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
monitoring_and_alerting: - Dashboard: KV reclamation overview (kv_epoch_lag, reclaimed_slabs_count, coalescer_throughput)
- Incident runbook updated with forced-drain and emergency-pid-restart steps
- Post-deploy automated smoke tests that run a short stress profile and validate no regressions
